clue.text: Writer's plagiarism in extremes of satire

indicators.note: the extremes of a word are its two end letters, so only the outside pair is kept
one thing set in another is placed inside it, so one piece goes within the other

blocks.note: to crib is to copy someone else's work, so a crib is a piece of plagiarism
the first and last letters of satire

explanation.surface: A writer is accused of copying material in the most extreme parts of a satirical piece.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's stands for 'is', joining the definition to the wordplay. CRIB sits between S and E.
explanation.definitionFit: A scribe is a person who writes, historically a copyist of manuscripts, so the word is a synonym for writer.

clue.text: Bans others playing low-pitched instrument

indicators.note: playing with something means toying with it, so these letters are moved about freely

blocks.note: the ten letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone forbids the rest of the band from playing a deep-toned instrument.
explanation.definitionFit: The basset horn is a member of the clarinet family pitched lower than the ordinary clarinet, used by Mozart.

clue.text: Turning up before remarriage essentially, express pleasure

indicators.note: turning a word round makes it read the other way, and in a down clue 'up' is read from the bottom
the essence of a word is its core, so only its central letters are kept
one piece placed before another simply comes first in the line of letters

blocks.note: the little word up, read backwards
the two central letters of this ten-letter word

explanation.surface: Someone turning up just ahead of a second wedding shows how happy they are about it.
explanation.walkthrough: Remarriage has ten letters, so its middle is the pair of letters in fifth and sixth place.
explanation.definitionFit: To purr is the contented sound a cat makes, and by extension any human murmur of satisfaction.

clue.text: Spiritual leader central to resisting and Hinduism

indicators.note: something central to a phrase sits in its middle, so the letters are found spanning the words

blocks.note: the run of letters straddling the three words

explanation.surface: A religious leader was at the heart of nonviolent resistance and of the Hindu faith.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer runs from the last letter of resisting, through and, into the start of Hinduism.
explanation.definitionFit: Mahatma Gandhi led India's independence movement and was revered as a moral and religious figure.

clue.text: Mysteries surrounding English releases

indicators.note: a thing surrounding another wraps around it, so the outer word encloses the other piece

blocks.note: mysteries are things kept hidden
standard abbreviation for English

explanation.surface: Puzzles involving the English are let out to the public.
explanation.walkthrough: E sits between SECRET and the final S.
explanation.definitionFit: A gland secretes a fluid when it discharges it, so the verb is a sense of giving out or releasing.

clue.text: Unnatural ugly hatred like offspring's behaviour

indicators.note: something unnatural is not in its normal form, so these letters are twisted out of their order

blocks.note: the ten letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Bitter loathing between relatives is hardly how children should behave.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests behaviour unlike a child's; in fact the definition describes conduct befitting a child.
explanation.definitionFit: Daughterly describes what is fitting for a daughter, a female child, so it is the way an offspring acts.

clue.text: Measure weak glue

blocks.note: first meaning: dimensions or magnitude
second meaning: a thin gelatinous wash used to seal paper or plaster

explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as an instruction to gauge an adhesive; the two halves are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both an object's bulk or dimensions and the dilute paste decorators brush on walls before papering.

clue.text: Reserve thing that torments enthusiastic reader

blocks.note: to book a table or seat is to reserve it
a worm is a gnawing source of torment, as in the biblical worm that never dies

explanation.surface: Someone books a place, though a nagging irritant keeps troubling them.
explanation.definitionFit: A bookworm is a person who reads avidly, named after the grubs that burrow through old volumes.

clue.text: Set in company hangout regularly tardy

indicators.note: taking letters regularly means taking them at even intervals, every other one

blocks.note: standard abbreviation for company
the second, fourth and sixth letters
tardy means late

explanation.surface: A group gathered in a firm's favourite haunt is always running late.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Regularly' applies only to hangout; tardy is defined, not thinned out.
explanation.definitionFit: To coagulate is to thicken from liquid into a solid mass, as jelly or blood does when it sets.

clue.text: French friend, good old buddy for Manuel, maybe

blocks.note: ami is French for friend
standard abbreviation for good
standard abbreviation for old

explanation.surface: A list of words for a pal in several languages, ending with a Spanish speaker's.
explanation.walkthrough: Manuel stands for any Spanish speaker; he is also the Spanish waiter in the British sitcom Fawlty Towers.
explanation.definitionFit: Amigo is the Spanish word for a friend, so it is what a Spaniard such as Manuel would call his pal.

clue.text: Nude sir? Not in order – covered!

indicators.note: letters that are not in order have been jumbled, so they must be rearranged

blocks.note: the seven letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A naked gentleman is told he is out of line and should cover himself up.
explanation.walkthrough: The joke is that covered seems to mean clothed; here it means protected by a policy.
explanation.definitionFit: Being insured means having a policy against loss, which is described as being covered.

clue.text: Tabloid with feeble-sounding charity event

indicators.note: sounding means the word is judged by how it is pronounced, not how it is written

blocks.note: a rag is a disparaging name for a low-quality newspaper
feeble means weak, which is pronounced like the seven-day period

explanation.surface: A popular newspaper teams up with a limp fundraising stunt.
explanation.walkthrough: Rag week is a British university tradition: a week of student stunts and collections raising money for charity.
explanation.definitionFit: Students hold a rag week each year to raise funds for good causes, so it is a fundraising event.

clue.text: Arranged exit terms for one with way-out political opinions

indicators.note: things arranged are put into a new order, so these letters are reordered

blocks.note: the nine letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Departure conditions were negotiated for a political radical.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Way-out' plays on exit: it means far from the mainstream here.
explanation.definitionFit: An extremist holds radical views far beyond the political mainstream, the sense of way-out as unconventional.

clue.text: Deprive of necessary content shattered tea service

indicators.note: something shattered is broken into fragments, so these letters are scattered and reassembled

blocks.note: the ten letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Smashing a tea set robs it of what it needs to hold.
explanation.definitionFit: To eviscerate is literally to disembowel, and figuratively to strip something of its vital substance.

clue.text: Utter disapproving sounds after thanks – it's just not done!

indicators.note: one piece coming after another follows it in the line of letters

blocks.note: ta is informal British for thanks
to boo is to jeer in disapproval

explanation.surface: Jeering after someone says thank you is simply bad manners.
explanation.definitionFit: A taboo is a social prohibition, something custom forbids, which is exactly what is not done.

clue.text: Warning sign to drivers: estate car, it's said, deficient in weight

indicators.note: it's said tells us to go by the spoken word rather than the written one

blocks.note: a shooting break is an old name for an estate car, a station wagon
something deficient in weight is light

explanation.surface: A notice for motorists about a station wagon that seems underweight.
explanation.walkthrough: Shooting break and shooting brake are both spellings of the estate car, so the sound links them.
explanation.definitionFit: Brake lights glow red at the back of a car to warn following drivers that it is slowing.

clue.text: Age-old game incorporating witchcraft and upper-class element

indicators.note: to incorporate is to take into the body, so the outer word holds the others inside it

blocks.note: nim is an ancient game of taking objects from heaps
obi (obeah) is a form of Caribbean sorcery
U is the old label for upper-class usage

explanation.surface: An ancient pastime involving magic and an aristocratic ingredient.
explanation.walkthrough: Nim is a game of removing counters from heaps, centuries old; obi, or obeah, is West Indian folk magic.
explanation.definitionFit: Niobium is a chemical element, a grey metal with atomic number 41 used in alloys.

clue.text: Formally propose observation about ancient weight of money

indicators.note: one thing about another goes around it, so the outer word wraps the other

blocks.note: a note is a remark or observation
the mina was an ancient Near Eastern weight and unit of currency

explanation.surface: Officially putting forward a comment about an old coinage measure.
explanation.definitionFit: To nominate someone is to put their name forward officially for a post or award.

clue.text: Stuff lifted roughly, including uncased solid earthenware

indicators.note: in a down clue something lifted is raised from bottom to top, so it reads upwards
removing the case of a word strips off its outer letters
including something means holding it within, so one piece is placed inside

blocks.note: to jam is to stuff or cram
ca is circa, Latin for about or roughly
the word solid, taken as written

explanation.surface: Material is carried up approximately, along with sturdy pottery taken out of its packing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stuff' and 'solid' look like nouns about material; one is a verb meaning cram, the other just loses its outer letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Majolica is tin-glazed Italian Renaissance pottery, a kind of decorated earthenware.

clue.text: Biting humour of a Roman Catholic during disorganised Mass

indicators.note: something disorganised is in disarray, so these letters are jumbled
something happening during another falls within it, so one piece goes inside

blocks.note: taken as written
standard abbreviation for Roman Catholic
the word Mass, taken as written

explanation.surface: A priest's cutting wit comes out during a chaotic church service.
explanation.walkthrough: Mass looks like a church word in the surface, but here it is only four letters to be jumbled.
explanation.definitionFit: Sarcasm is cutting, mocking irony, so it is wit that bites or wounds.

clue.text: Ludicrously energetic fellow in command

blocks.note: a fellow is a man
IC is short for in charge or in command

explanation.surface: A frantic, overexcited man is the one giving the orders.
explanation.definitionFit: Manic describes wild, frenzied activity, an excessive and almost absurd level of energy.

clue.text: Sweet semi-solid dessert and vegetable

blocks.note: jelly is a wobbly set pudding
a bean is a vegetable

explanation.surface: A pudding of set jelly served with a side of greens.
explanation.walkthrough: In British English a sweet is a candy, not just a dessert, and jelly is what Americans call Jell-O.
explanation.definitionFit: A jelly bean is a small bean-shaped chewy candy, so it is a sweet in British usage.

clue.text: Prettily ornamental, holding, for example, inherited thing

indicators.note: a word holding another keeps it within, so the outer word wraps around

blocks.note: lacy means delicately decorative
eg is the abbreviation meaning for example

explanation.surface: Delicate, decorative pieces, for instance, are the heirloom passed down.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole phrase 'for example' gives EG; 'for' is shared between that phrase and the link here, so it is listed as a link only.
explanation.definitionFit: A legacy is something left to a person in a will or passed down from a predecessor.

clue.text: Very old yet tipsily found after inn runs amok

indicators.note: something done tipsily is unsteady and muddled, so these letters stagger out of order
a thing that runs amok goes wild, so its letters are scrambled
one piece found after another follows it in the line of letters

blocks.note: the word inn, taken as written
the word yet, taken as written

explanation.surface: A very aged drinker is still found staggering about after the pub goes wild.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who is ninety years of age is regarded as very elderly, so the age stands for great age.

clue.text: Indifferent about nervous system disrupted by start of trouble

indicators.note: the start of a word is its first letter, so only that is kept
something disrupted by an intruder has it break in, so one letter goes inside

blocks.note: neural means relating to the nerves
the first letter of trouble

explanation.surface: Someone unconcerned about their nerves until a hint of trouble upsets them.
explanation.walkthrough: T goes into NEURAL after its fourth letter.
explanation.definitionFit: To be neutral is to take no side, which is being impartial or unconcerned about the outcome.

clue.text: Employs tricks with no reason principally

indicators.note: principally means chiefly, pointing to the first letter of the word
with no means lacking something, so that letter is taken away

blocks.note: ruses are tricks or stratagems
the first letter of reason

explanation.surface: Someone resorts to underhand methods without any good grounds.
explanation.walkthrough: RUSES loses its R.
explanation.definitionFit: To use something is to employ it, putting it into service, so uses matches employs as a verb.

clue.text: Man one pursues with an alpine plant

indicators.note: one that pursues another follows behind it, coming next in the letters

blocks.note: a gent is a man
the Roman numeral for one
taken as written

explanation.surface: A single person chases after a man in the mountains, botanically speaking.
explanation.definitionFit: The gentian is a mountain flower, famed for its intense blue trumpet blooms in the Alps.

clue.text: Exigency once held intermittently

indicators.note: something done intermittently stops and starts, so letters are taken at intervals

blocks.note: the even letters of the two words

explanation.surface: An urgent requirement that was once gripped only now and then.
explanation.definitionFit: An exigency is a pressing demand or urgent requirement, which is a need.

clue.text: Deal with unfinished negotiation

indicators.note: something unfinished lacks its ending, so the final letter is dropped

blocks.note: a treaty is a negotiated agreement

explanation.surface: Handling a negotiation that has not yet concluded.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Deal' tempts as a noun matching negotiation, but the definition is the verb phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: To treat a matter is to handle or address it, the same sense as dealing with it.

clue.text: Strutting leader hated circling in old-fashioned headgear

indicators.note: circling means going round in a loop, so letters from one end are carried round to the other

blocks.note: a cock is a strutting bird and a leader, as in cock of the walk
the word hated, taken as written

explanation.surface: The swaggering boss everyone despised went round wearing a quaint hat.
explanation.walkthrough: The last two letters of HATED move round to the front.
explanation.definitionFit: A cocked hat has its brim turned up on two or three sides, the tricorn style of the eighteenth century.
